<!--
Write this description for a reviewer who did not watch the work happen.
Authors and coding agents: use natural, concise prose. Summarize outcomes
instead of narrating every command. Give the reasoning and context a
reviewer actually needs. Avoid repetitive headings, bullet dumps, and
machine-style status reports. Name files or implementation details only
when they help the reviewer understand the change or its risk. Keep
Validation to meaningful evidence, not every trivial command. Write
`None` when a section genuinely has nothing useful to add.
-->

## What changed
Briefly explain the actual change and the problem it solves.

## Why
Explain why this change is useful or necessary.

## Validation
Describe the meaningful checks performed.

## Notes
Anything reviewers should know — tradeoffs, limitations, follow-up work — or `None`.
